title: The Open Compass
premise: Yara Pemberton has spent seven years flying medicine and secrets across the northern interior, keeping every settlement at arm's length because the last people she stayed for didn't survive her staying. When a record low tide exposes a sea cave that local legends say 'charges admission,' Yara and geologist Teodor Vance are trapped inside by a rockfall and discover an expedition's remains — and evidence of something worth killing to keep quiet. Rescued but bound together, they must guide the cave's surviving discoverers home through a storm season while deciding whether the truth in their hands belongs to the world or to the dead who paid for it. In the end, Yara chooses truth over safety, loses her wings and her anonymity, and gains for the first time a place — and people — worth stopping for.
about_author: Mara Galloway is the pen name of a former floatplane dispatcher who spent a decade logging weather delays and last words from the far north. She writes adventure fiction about people whose survival depends on what they refuse to say.

chapters.title: Fuel, Weather, Rumors
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A supply run into Kestrel Bay introduces her rule: land, unload, leave before anyone learns your name. A passenger, geologist Teodor Vance, talks too much about a tide chart anomaly on the coast. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Wouldn't Land
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. He hires Yara against her better judgment to overfly a stretch of coast where his late mentor's expedition vanished eleven years ago. Yara refuses the job but can't stop reading the coordinates he leaves behind. Beat: curiosity as a threat to survival.

chapters.title: Lowest Tide in Forty Years
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Flying solo, she breaks her own rule and diverts to the coast. The receded sea reveals a black archway in the cliff — the cave of legend. She lands on the tidal shelf just as Teodor's chartered boat arrives uninvited. Beat: the moment caution fails.

chapters.title: Admission
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Inside the cave: carved markers, rusted gear, and a sealed field case bearing Teodor's mentor's initials. The tide turns early; the exit floods; a rockfall seals the inner passage. Beat: wonder curdling into entrapment.

chapters.title: What the Dead Were Carrying
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. By headlamp they find the 2013 expedition's camp — three bodies, one empty sleeping bag, and core samples that shouldn't exist this far north. Teodor recognizes sabotage, not accident. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Empty Sleeping Bag
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A survivor walked out — and someone has been leaving fresh supplies at the cave mouth for years. Yara realizes the legends were maintained deliberately, like a fence around a secret. Beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. They blast a secondary vent open with flare compound and crawl out onto the shelf as the tide returns, losing the field case to the water — except the samples Teodor pocketed. Beat: escape bought with evidence they can't unknow.

chapters.title: Debrief Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Back in Kestrel Bay, a company man named Aldous Reeve meets their plane before the wheels stop spinning, offering hush money and a story about unstable cliffs. Yara takes the money out of habit. Beat: complicity arriving dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: Two Truths in One Tank
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. Teodor confronts Yara about the bribe; she argues silence keeps them alive. Their fight cracks open her past — the settlement fire she flew away from. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: The Third Survivor
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. An old trapper named Sif Halvorsen, keeper of the cave legend, summons Yara: she is the empty sleeping bag, and the supplies were hers. She warns that Reeve's employer caused the 2013 rockfall. Beat: the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: Storm Season Opens Early
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. Weather closes the interior passes; the samples must reach a university lab before Reeve's people recover them. Yara agrees to fly the impossible window — not for truth, she claims, but because Sif asked. Beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Tailwind of Lies
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Mid-flight, Yara discovers Reeve's tracker sewn into the sample case. She must choose: dump the evidence, or fly a decoy route through the worst weather in a decade. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Whiteout Over the Divide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The decoy run nearly kills them both; a forced landing on a frozen lake strands them overnight. In the dark, Yara finally tells the whole story of the fire — and why she stopped belonging anywhere. Beat: intimacy forged in cold.

chapters.title: What Reeve Knows
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV (first antagonist chapter). Reeve reports to his employer, revealing the 2013 expedition found a mineral strike worth billions — and that orders were to bury it with its finders. He requests permission to handle Yara 'permanently.' Beat: stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Sif's Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Sif gives them her eleven-year ledger of payments and deliveries — proof of the cover-up — then burns her own cabin to erase her tracks, asking only that the truth outlive her. Beat: sacrifice as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Run for the Coast
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. A chase sequence: Reeve's men pursue the pair across the tundra toward a coastal airstrip. Teodor splits off as bait, carrying the decoy case, trusting Yara with the real samples. Beat: trust as an act of faith.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Teodor is caught; Yara escapes with the evidence but learns Reeve will trade him for it. Her old instinct says fly away. Instead she turns back toward the bay. Beat: the climactic reversal — staying costs everything, and she pays.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Low Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the cave mouth at extreme low tide, Yara offers the trade — then springs her plan: she's already broadcast Sif's ledger and the sample data to every radio operator on the coast. The secret is out; the leverage is gone. Beat: climax.

chapters.title: Rockfall, Reversed
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reeve tries to seal the truth — and the witnesses — inside the collapsing cave, echoing 2013. Yara and a freed Teodor lead him out at gunpoint of conscience rather than weapon, letting the tide and his employers do the rest. Beat: justice without vengeance.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. The inquiry: Yara testifies, surrendering her license for the illegal flights, naming names including her own compromises. The mineral strike becomes protected land. Beat: truth's cost counted honestly.

chapters.title: A Name Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Grounded for a year, Yara stays in Kestrel Bay — teaching Sif's grandniece to read weather, fixing the lodge, being known. For the first time, stopping doesn't feel like dying. Beat: belonging earned.

chapters.title: The Open Compass
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Yara's POV. Her license restored, she flies the medicine run again — but now she lingers, lands, stays for supper. The compass needle no longer points only away. Final image: the cave entrance above the tide line, marked honestly at last. Beat: resolution and peace.
